Butter Chicken!!  Ingredients The chicken 2 lb chicken breast or thigh, cut into bite size pieces ⅓ cup greek yogurt  2 tsp kashmiri chile powder 2 tsp garam masala  1 ½ tsp turmeric  2 tsp garlic grated  2 tsp ginger grated 1 tsp fenugreek leaves 1 Tbsp olive oil The juice of 1 lemon 1 tsp salt The sauce 3 Tbsp ghee 4 cardamom pods 4 cloves 1 piece of cinnamon stick 4 cloves garlic, sliced 1 inch knob ginger, sliced 1 green chile, minced 24 oz crushed tomatoes ⅓ raw cashews  1 tsp kashmiri chile powder 2 tsp garam masala  1 cup cream 1 tsp fenugreek leaves Salt to taste To start in a bowl add the yogurt, kashmiri chile powder, garam masala, turmeric, garlic, ginger, fenugreek leaves, olive oil, lemon and salt. Mix well then add the chicken mix again, then add to a wire rack lined sheet tray, spread it into one layer. Broil for about 10 minutes until lightly charred. For the sauce in a large pan over medium high heat add the ghee then toast the spices for 2 minutes. Then remove them. Add the chili, garlic and ginger. Cook for 1-2 until fragrant. Add the tomatoes and cashews, simmer for 10 minutes then blend until smooth. Add that back to the pan and add cream, kashmiri chili powder, garam masala, fenugreek and salt to taste. Add the chicken into the sauce and reheat it for 2-3 minutes. Serve with garlic naan and garnish with cilantro.  Enjoy!!

First time hatching chickens and today I learnt a VERY important lesson… the hard way 😅🐣 Apparently when you decide to spontaneously let two broody hens hatch eggs, put another lot in an incubator and basically just hope for the best… you should probably be checking on everyone a little more closely. 😂 Because today I realised I’d made a pretty vital mistake. One of my broody girls had gotten off her nest… and I have absolutely no idea when. 🫠 I went out to check on everyone and found her happily sitting in a completely different nesting box, while her 7 developing eggs were sitting there cold. And my stomach DROPPED. These aren’t freshly laid eggs either. We’ve candled them. We’ve seen veins. We’ve seen movement. There are actually tiny little chicks developing in there. 🥺 From what I can work out, she could have been off them anywhere from around 12–24 hours. So now we’re in the horrible little waiting game of “did I just lose 7 chicks, or are these tiny things much tougher than I think?” 😭 I’ve put her back on the correct nest and she’s settled straight back down like absolutely nothing happened… meanwhile I’m hovering around like an anxious first-time chicken midwife. 😂 This whole hatching experiment has been such a massive learning curve. I’ve learnt about candling, humidity, incubator temperatures, broody hens, moving nests, fertility, lockdown… and now apparently I can add “MAKE SURE THE BROODY HEN IS ACTUALLY SITTING ON THE RIGHT EGGS” to the list. 🤦🏼‍♀️😂 But I guess that’s the reality of learning as you go. This was completely spontaneous. I’ve never hatched chicks before. I didn’t start this knowing exactly what I was doing, and I’m definitely going to make mistakes along the way. For now, I’m leaving the eggs alone, letting Mumma do her thing and crossing absolutely EVERYTHING that when we candle them again there’s still life in there. 🤞🏼🐣 If they make it through being abandoned and going cold for potentially an entire day, these are officially going to be the toughest little Backyard Busy Brains chickens ever. 😂 We’re getting so close to hatch day now too, which somehow makes this even more stressful. So… place your bets. 🐣 Do you think they’ll still hatch? 🥚 How many of the 7 do you think will make it? 🐓 And while we’re at it — how many do we reckon will inevitably be roosters? 😂 Because apparently my first attempt at hatching chicks needed a little extra ✨drama✨. I’ll update after the next candle… please cross your fingers for our little eggs. 🤞🏼🥹🐣 #mistake #eggs #chickens #farmlife #fyp

My chickens have started undressing for fall. 😂 Molting season is starting in my flock, which means I’m finding chicken feathers EVERYWHERE around the coop and run. Molting is the natural process of shedding old, worn feathers and growing a fresh new set. Adult chickens typically molt once a year, often in late summer or fall as the days begin getting shorter. During a molt, you may notice: 🪶 Feathers all over the coop and run 🪶 Scruffy or patchy-looking hens 🪶 New pin feathers growing in 🪶 Egg production slowing down or stopping 🪶 Chickens acting a little quieter than usual And some chickens barely look like they’re molting while others look absolutely ragged. 😂 Are your chickens are starting to molt too? 🐔🪶 #chickens #backyardchickens #molting #raisingchickens #chickensoftiktok
